# Create Knowledge Note

Capture detailed thought-leadership IP: why, what, how, evidence, boundaries, lineage, examples, and reusable practices.

## Input and source rules

Require source material. A brief may be supplied or developed interactively.

Treat sources in this order: existing canonical note, approved IP, transcript/notes, then clearly identified synthesis. Preserve exact terminology; separate evidence, opinion, interpretation, recommendation, and hypothesis; acknowledge lineage; never fabricate quotes or certainty.

Read [references/authoring-guide.md](references/authoring-guide.md) for the deterministic analysis, option matrices, contract fields, writing rules, extraction map, and metadata format.

## Mandatory interaction gate

**Do not draft or modify the note immediately after reading the source.**

1. Read all sources and build the IP inventory.
2. Present the candidate concept map.
3. Ask what to keep, drop, park, or merge. Offer **No opinion — recommend**, **All of them**, and **None — reanalyse**.
4. Propose two to four point-of-view options with central claim, tension, audience, stakes, contribution, lineage, boundaries, and desired change.
5. Refine one focused question at a time. Complementary viewpoints may share a note; separate theses require separate notes.
6. Present the knowledge-note contract.
7. Obtain explicit approval. Approval of concepts alone is not approval to write.

## Authoring

After approval:

1. Establish the canonical thesis, vocabulary, framework, practices, examples, boundaries, and claim status.
2. Run the integrity checks in the authoring guide.
3. Write from [assets/knowledge-note-template.md](assets/knowledge-note-template.md).
4. Write ideas directly for a private knowledge base—never as a workshop report or document-production narrative.
5. Add the downstream extraction map and invisible metadata footer.

When revising, update rather than duplicate the note, increment its version, preserve stable terminology, and identify stale downstream assets.

## Completion

The task is complete only when the user approved the concepts and point of view, the note is understandable without the source transcript, claims and synthesis are distinguishable, terminology is consistent, limitations are explicit, and downstream assets can reuse the IP without redefining it.
